news.Title: 5 big analyst AI moves: Muse AI seen as major catalyst for Meta; MSFT upgraded
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Here are the biggest analyst moves in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for this week.

Still guessing which names to buy? Our AI rebuilds its stock picks at the start of every month. The list is beating the market by 120%. See what's on it »

Stifel upgrades Microsoft to Buy, says it "clearly turned the corner"

Stifel this week upgraded Microsoft stock to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $575 from $530, voicing increasing confidence that the company can sustain mid-to-upper-teens revenue growth.

Analysts led by Brad Reback said Microsoft "clearly turned the corner post the June quarter print," pointing to sustained Azure upside, reduced large-language-model research intensity and accelerating contribution from OpenAI.

Stifel expects 200 to 300 basis points of further Azure upside as Microsoft achieves "a more sustained efficiency cadence across the stack from silicon, models and software," aided by CFO Amy Hood's disclosure that Microsoft has cut "dock-to-live times" by more than 50% over the past year, helping capacity convert to revenue faster.

Copilot seat count reached roughly 30 million in the fourth quarter, up 10 million quarter-over-quarter, while GitHub's shift to consumption-based pricing adds another growth lever. These tailwinds should offset moderating seat growth as Microsoft 365 approaches 500 million seats, sustaining at least mid-teens growth for several years, the analysts said.

Earlier concerns about margin compression proved "too negative," the analysts said, pointing to Azure efficiency gains, the elimination of revenue-share payments to OpenAI after an April contract revision, and an extension of asset useful life to 25 years from 15. Microsoft's need to aggressively invest in its own large-language-model development is also "abating" as open-weight models deliver comparable outcomes at lower cost.

Buy weakness in stocks as AI trade set to continue: Citi

Citi remains overweight equities led by the U.S., saying it would add more stock market exposure if shares pull back, even as higher oil prices, rising rates and poor seasonals weigh on sentiment.

"We are impressed how well the equity market has been trading in the light of higher oil, higher rates, and poor seasonals in Sep, even at a time when volatility in U.S. rates is rising," the bank's strategists wrote in their September house views. They noted stocks usually pull back after the Fed's first rate hike rather than before it, and that markets also tend to weaken ahead of midterm elections before the usual year-end rally.

Story Continues

"We prefer the U.S. as we still believe that the AI trade will continue," the strategists wrote, adding that the U.S. is also better protected from further rises in oil prices. Emerging Asia, cut in early July, is Citi's next choice when it adds risk.

In bonds, Citi remains neutral on duration, long emerging markets and short European government bonds. The upcoming French election adds to European risks, and the bank moved U.K. gilts back to neutral. "At this stage, it is unclear to us what it will take to stop a hawkish Fed," the strategists said.

Citi stayed underweight investment-grade credit in the U.S. and Europe as a hedge for its equity overweight. In commodities, it remains long base metals and neutral on energy, having recently cut its gold long, and moved emerging market currencies back to neutral given rising U.S. rate volatility.

Wall Street positive on Meta as Muse AI agent emerges as key growth driver

Wall Street analysts were broadly positive on Meta following its Connect event, where the company made its Muse AI agent the centerpiece of its product and hardware plans.

Evercore ISI kept its Outperform rating and $860 price target, calling Meta its top long idea. "Muse over Metaverse is a good thing for META investors," the analysts wrote, adding that Muse could lead investors to value the stock at 25 to 30 times 2028 earnings, taking shares to $1,000 or more.

The broker compared the moment to Alphabet's own AI transition: "Just like GOOGL in 2025, what we are witnessing is a transition from a perceived 'AI Loser' to an 'AI Winner.'"

Raymond James analyst Josh Beck raised his price target to $860, based on 20 times 2028 earnings, citing Muse downloads of more than 300,000 a day and a base case of more than $50 billion in revenue against annual costs of about $12 billion.

Separately, Mizuho's Lloyd Walmsley, who has an Outperform rating and $750 target, said Muse Charm — a keychain-like device expected before the holidays — could accelerate user growth further. "Meta's AI product has significant momentum," he wrote, though he was more cautious on Meta's new $1,299 VR glasses due to their high price.

Citi also kept its Buy rating and $800 target, saying it is more positive on the shares after the event, while JPMorgan said Muse could become the most widely used consumer AI app since ChatGPT.

Citi raises Micron target to $1,300, expects shares to rally into SEMICON West

In a separate note, Citi has raised its price target on Micron to $1,300 from $1,150, expecting the stock to rally into the SEMICON West conference and anticipating upside to results and guidance when the company reports.

The bank lifted its August and November-quarter estimates on better-than-expected blended DRAM pricing, now modeling fiscal fourth-quarter sales and EPS of $51 billion and $31.45, above consensus. Micron's stock "has made a large round trip since last earnings, falling 35% from the prior high and rebounding 34% from the July low," Citi analysts said, pointing to SEMICON West as the next catalyst.

At the conference, Citi anticipates equipment makers will flag shortages of DRAM, MLCC, printed circuit boards and optical components, a potential bottleneck in the tools used to manufacture memory chips. Those constraints could limit DRAM and NAND supply growth to the low-20% range and help push memory prices higher into next year, with both markets expected to remain undersupplied on strong AI-driven demand and prices likely peaking in Q2 2027.

Citi assumes blended DRAM average selling prices rise 20% and 13% quarter-on-quarter in the current and following periods, with NAND up 34% and 15%, and expects enterprise SSD demand driven by AI inference to offset softer consumer NAND.

Rosenblatt starts Sandisk at Buy, says AI is turning NAND into critical infrastructure

Also this week, Rosenblatt initiated coverage of SanDisk with a Buy rating and a $2,400 price target, arguing that AI is transforming NAND flash memory from a commodity into a critical piece of computing infrastructure.

Analyst Kevin Cassidy said new AI compute platforms are creating an opportunity to reposition NAND "from a commodity storage medium to a more system-critical component of AI infrastructure," as expanding model sizes and data-intensive inference prioritize density, performance, endurance and supply certainty over the lowest price.

Cassidy pointed to SanDisk's BiCS8 and BiCS10 platforms, developed with manufacturing partner Kioxia over some 25 years, as supporting that shift — improving density with fewer 3D layers than some rivals, sustaining a cost and performance advantage in AI-oriented enterprise storage.

New business model agreements with eight of the largest NAND customers, potentially covering about 65% of fiscal 2028 production, should improve demand visibility and reduce historical sector volatility, he added.

Management's fiscal 2028-to-2030 framework calls for mid-to-high-teens revenue growth, roughly 80% non-GAAP gross margin and a 50% adjusted free-cash-flow margin. Cassidy conservatively estimated fiscal 2030 non-GAAP earnings of about $300 a share.

His $2,400 target is based on 10 times his fiscal 2028 earnings estimate, a multiple he called conservative given the growth outlook, while reflecting execution risk and the chance NAND reverts to cyclical, commodity-like pricing.

news.Title: Azure’s Inflection Point: Can Microsoft (MSFT) Balance AI Growth With Capex Risk?
news.Content:
Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ) has lagged the broader market amid growing concerns about ballooning capital expenditure. The stock is up roughly 5% year to date, compared with a gain of about 21% for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100, which has bounced to record levels.

Investors have also been weighing Microsoft's capital allocation strategy, particularly after its latest dividend increase. For a deeper look at how the company's AI spending could affect its dividend investment thesis, see: Microsoft (MSFT) Raises Its Dividend 8%. Does AI Spending Change the Investment Case?

However, the sentiment surrounding the stock may be starting to improve. In a September 23 research note, Stifel reiterated its view that robust growth in artificial intelligence and other strategic initiatives could strengthen the company's growth outlook. The firm upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $575 from $530.

Stifel believes Microsoft can sustain revenue growth in the mid-to-upper teens while maintaining relatively stable operating margins. The firm also expects improving operational efficiencies to support strong cash flow, potentially reducing Microsoft's need to seek external financing to fund its investments.

Azure Remains a Key Growth Driver

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has reached an important inflection point, supported by continued strength in its Azure cloud-computing business. Stifel believes Azure's recent acceleration can continue as additional data-center capacity becomes available. Operational efficiencies, additional data-center capacity and a growing revenue contribution from OpenAI could also support Azure's growth.

The sentiment comes on the heels of CFO Amy Hood saying efficiency gains are being monetized quickly amid strong demand, while process improvements have shortened the lead time for bringing CPU and GPU capacity online. This makes Microsoft's existing AI infrastructure more productive.

Microsoft is also expanding its AI monetization opportunities. Copilot seats reached roughly 30 million in the fiscal fourth quarter, while GitHub's transition toward consumption-based pricing provides another potential source of recurring growth. These developments could help Microsoft capture more value from its expanding AI ecosystem.

Microsoft's AI Investment Comes With Risks

Amid the bullish thesis and price target hike Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) still faces risks that could affect the stock's momentum. For starters, it still faces high capital requirements to strengthen its AI and data center capacity, which could eat into margins.

Story Continues

Rapid advances in rival AI models could make it more difficult for Microsoft to maintain premium pricing for Azure AI services and Copilot. Although Copilot adoption has expanded rapidly, converting a large user base into durable incremental revenue and profits remains an important challenge.

Hedge Fund Positioning

Meanwhile, hedge fund positioning toward Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) weakened modestly between the first and second quarters, with the number of hedge funds holding the stock declining from 282 to 273.

However, several large investors continued to increase their exposure. According to Insider Monkey's database, Arrowstreet Capital raised its Microsoft stake by 14% to approximately $10.31 billion, while Fisher Asset Management increased its position by 3% to roughly $9.92 billion.

Short interest also declined. Approximately 67.35 million Microsoft shares were sold short as of September 15, down from 68.54 million shares as of August 14. Short interest remained relatively limited at about 0.91% of shares outstanding, indicating that the stock is not heavily positioned for a decline.

The Verdict

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)'s investment case is increasingly centered on whether strong Azure growth and faster AI monetization can offset the enormous cost of building the infrastructure needed to support the next phase of cloud and AI expansion.

At the same time, elevated capital expenditures, intensifying AI competition, and uncertainty around Copilot monetization remain important risks for investors to monitor. The balance between Microsoft's massive AI investments and the revenue and cash flow they ultimately generate will likely remain a key factor in the stock's performance.

While we acknowledge the potential of MSFT as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Meta misled users about Facebook data practices, New Mexico jury finds
news.Content:
By Diana Novak Jones

Sept 25 (Reuters) - A jury in Santa Fe, New Mexico, found on Friday that Meta Platforms misled the state's residents in a case arising from allegations that a political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent.

The ‌verdict followed a two-week trial over a lawsuit filed by New Mexico's attorney general in 2021, three years after news reports revealed that the firm, Cambridge Analytica, ‌had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

A Meta spokesperson said the company disagreed with the verdict and would continue to defend itself "against efforts to distort our record."

"Meta's platforms are ​forums for free expression," the spokesperson said. "We have a First Amendment right to manage those platforms in a way we believe best serves the interests of our community. This means prioritizing free speech, protecting our users' information and giving them control over their data."

At a press conference after the verdict was announced, New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said the case revealed "in stark detail the way in which this company plays fast and loose with the rules."

The state accused Meta of misleading New Mexicans about how it shared user data with third parties and enforced policies on hate ‌speech and misinformation. New Mexico argued that Facebook failed to disclose ⁠that it sold user data to outside parties and allowed harmful content to spread when doing so benefited the company's bottom line.

Jurors found 26 of 29 statements identified by the state were misleading, including comments about user data, hate speech and misinformation. They rejected claims that Meta misled ⁠consumers in statements about its efforts to remove harmful content and its fact-checking practices.

MAXIMUM PENALTY SOUGHT

Judge Francis Mathew will now determine civil penalties after jurors found more than 43 million violations, based on the number of people affected by the company's misleading statements. Under New Mexico law, Mathew can award up to $5,000 per violation.

Torrez said his office is evaluating how much to seek but will push for the ​maximum ​penalty based on the jury's findings.

The state will also ask Mathew to direct Meta to make changes, ​which could include corrections to its past misstatements as well as an ‌audit of the way it manages user data, Torrez said.

MISLEADING CLAIMS DETAILED

The state's lawsuit focused on specific statements, including comments made by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg or in company blog posts, that New Mexico said made people believe they had control over the personal information they shared on the site, or that the site had blanket policies for how it dealt with hate speech or misinformation. Meta was selling the data to third-party apps, like the one that Cambridge Analytica relied on, and had exceptions to its policies for certain users, the state said.

Story Continues

Attorneys for Meta had argued at trial that the allegedly misleading statements were cherry-picked snippets that ignored critical context from the same statements, in which the company had repeatedly acknowledged its handling of ‌misinformation or privacy issues was not perfect.

Meta also denied that it sells users' information.

Reuters viewed the trial on ​Courtroom View Network.

EARLIER NEW MEXICO CASE

The verdict marks the second time in six months a jury in Santa ​Fe has weighed a lawsuit brought by the state of New Mexico against Meta ​Platforms.

In the first trial, which ended in March, a Santa Fe jury found Meta misled users about young users' safety on its Facebook, Instagram ‌and WhatsApp platforms and ordered the company to pay $375 million in civil ​penalties. After a second phase of that trial, a ​judge directed the company to pay $567 million into a New Mexico fund for teen mental health and ordered Meta to implement measures to protect teen Facebook and Instagram users in New Mexico.

A few weeks after the judge's ruling, Meta reached a sweeping settlement with 47 US states, Washington, D.C., and US territories, agreeing to pay a maximum ​of about $16.7 billion to resolve claims that it designed Facebook and ‌Instagram to addict young children. As part of that deal, it agreed to pay a handful of states that had sued the company over privacy violations ​related to Cambridge Analytica $459 million to resolve those cases.

New Mexico was not part of the settlement, so its case over Cambridge Analytica moved forward to trial.

(Reporting ​by Diana Novak Jones in Chicago; Editing by Alexia Garamfalvi, Nia Williams and Matthew Lewis)

news.Title: Evercore ISI’s Bullish iPhone Survey Faces a Reality Check From Pre-Order Data
news.Content:
Evercore ISI's annual consumer survey points to the strongest iPhone upgrade intent in years, with pricing power appearing to be even stronger than unit volume. The findings were strong enough for the firm to raise its price target. While the survey is detailed and supported by historical comparisons, it measures what consumers said they intended to do before the launch. Actual pre-order data for the iPhone 18 now provides a different data point. JP Morgan's initial delivery lead-time tracking shows shorter wait times than last year, particularly in China.

Despite the positive analyst sentiment surrounding the latest iPhone launch, AAPL stock is facing $2.7 billion worth of pressure from an unlikely source .

Evercore ISI's Survey Points To a Stronger-Than-Normal iPhone Upgrade Cycle

Evercore ISI found strong iPhone buying intentions in its survey of nearly 4,000 consumers, with 61% saying they plan to purchase an iPhone this year. That is the second-strongest result in the survey's history and well above its 45% long-term average. Demand also shifted toward higher-end models, with 53% saying they planned to buy an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, above Evercore ISI's 51% survey average. Another 14% said they planned to purchase the new iPhone Duo. Analyst Amit Daryanani said pricing was the bigger surprise:

Pricing trends continued to grow, with our survey reflecting an aggregate ASP of $1,374, up nearly 28% and well above our long-term survey average.

The firm raised its Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL ) price target from $365 to $380 while keeping an Outperform rating.

Real-World Data Offers a More Mixed Picture

Early iPhone 18 data initially showed shorter delivery waits than the previous generation. However, that gap closed quickly, with JP Morgan's tracking showing global lead times for the Pro and Pro Max expanding by 12 and 7 days, respectively, in the days following the September 12 pre-order launch. By mid-week, the Pro Max's wait time had converged with last year's iPhone 17 cycle. JP Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee attributed the initially shorter lead times to Apple front-loading premium inventory early in the cycle rather than to weaker demand, so the lead-time data on its own doesn't clearly support a softer-demand read. However, GF Securities separately described early demand as lukewarm and pricing tells a more consistent story. The iPhone 18 Pro's actual starting price increased by only $100.

Evercore ISI's survey confirms strong consumer interest in the iPhone 18 lineup, but the pre-order data doesn't clearly challenge that enthusiasm. With JP Morgan's lead-time signal now neutralized, the bigger question is pricing. Consumers said they would accept significantly higher costs, but Evercore's pricing thesis also depends on buyers shifting toward higher-end models and storage configurations.

Story Continues

Hedge fund ownership of Apple remained virtually unchanged, with the number of funds holding the stock slipping from 170 at the end of Q1 2026 to 169 at the end of the second quarter of 2026. The negligible move points to stable institutional sentiment, while short interest stood at only 0.80% of float.

For both retail and institutional investors, the iPhone upgrade cycle continues to be significant, especially as the latest AI features may not be available on previous generations. Despite criticism of a lack of innovation over the last couple of years, the company continues to win customer upgrades to the latest iPhone models.

While we acknowledge the potential of AAPL as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Tesla begins delivering Semi trucks to customers after years of delays
news.Content:
Tesla on Thursday announced that the electric vehicle maker was beginning deliveries of its Semi trucks to customers this week.

Executives at Tesla's plant in Sparks, Nevada, made the announcement that the first customers will take delivery of the electric big rigs about nine years after CEO Elon Musk first announced the company's plans to develop the long-haul freight trucks.

The Semi aims to open a new market for Tesla, which has long been known for its EV sedans and SUVs, by creating an electric option for commercial freight haulers.

The announcement comes at a time when diesel prices have surged to record highs, raising costs on firms in the trucking industry.

Tesla Reopens Roadster Reservations – But You'll Need $50K

Tesla didn't disclose its plans for production volumes of the Semi or its pricing at a webcast event held late Thursday at the plant, though it reiterated plans to build 50,000 Semis a year at the Nevada facility.

Read On The Fox Business App

Elon Musk wasn't in attendance at the event but said in a recorded video message that, "I'd recommend placing more orders if you haven't already, but the waiting list is already pretty significant.

Several companies that have purchased the Semi – including PepsiCo , DHL and U.S. Foods – were in attendance at the Tesla event and were invited on stage, while trucks with their logos were shown outside.

The long-range variant of the Semi has a range of 500 miles with a single charge, as Tesla director of Semi truck engineering Dan Priestly said, those are "500 real-world miles. Our customers have validated it." The standard version of the Semi has a shorter range of 325 miles on a single charge.

Tesla Files Plans For Proposed $10.1B Texas Solar Manufacturing Plant

Tesla and Musk first unveiled the Semi in 2017 and planned to start production in 2019, though it faced delays due to supply chain disruptions.

The first Semi was delivered to U.S. customers, including PepsiCo, in late 2022 – though those trucks were made on Tesla's lower-volume pilot production lines.

The EV maker's first truck rolled off the high-volume production line in April. While volume production was expected to start this year, Tesla has since adjusted that guidance to not explicitly state that it will reach high-volume production this year.

Tesla's Electric Semi-truck Takes On Diesel Big Rig

Despite delays, competition and shifts in EV policy in the U.S., Tesla received a new order for 2,500 Semis from a coalition of major cargo-owning shipping companies – including Microsoft and PepsiCo, according to the nonprofit Catalyst Mobility. The group noted that figure is nearly double the existing fleet of electric Class 8 trucks.

Additionally, Swedish freight technology company Einride announced a deal last week to add 500 Semi trucks to its fleet.

Reuters contributed to this report.

Original article source: Tesla begins delivering Semi trucks to customers after years of delays

news.Title: Meet the Magnificent Semiconductor Stock Crushing Nvidia in 2026
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) has been one of the market's most popular stocks over the past few years. With a market capitalization of over $5.45 trillion, it's the world's most valuable public company, aided by its 21% gains so far this year (as of Sept. 23).

Despite Nvidia's impressive returns this year, it doesn't compare to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) (TSMC), which is up over 46%. The semiconductor giant has a lucrative relationship with Nvidia, and right now, its business is capitalizing more than ever.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

TSMC is critical to the tech ecosystem

TSMC is the world's largest semiconductor foundry. Its foundry business model means that instead of making chips for general sale, it makes chips for companies' specific products.

For example, Nvidia's GPUs have become critical to the current AI boom (which is largely why the company has become so valuable); however, Nvidia doesn't actually make them. It designs them, and TSMC manufactures and brings them to life.

Manufacturing chips is hard and expensive, and it requires a lot of expertise. That's why companies instead rely on TSMC -- which has been doing it since 1987. TSMC is the go-to manufacturer for Nvidia, Apple , Microsoft , Alphabet , Amazon , and almost every major tech company.

High demand comes with high pricing power

TSMC's business has thrived for a while, but the current AI arms race has done wonders for it. As companies spend billions to build data centers and other AI infrastructure, demand for TSMC's manufacturing capabilities has grown. This has given TSMC unmatched pricing power and sent profits soaring.

In the second quarter, TSMC's revenue rose 33.7% year over year to $40.2 billion, but more impressive is how much its margins have expanded. Over the past year, its gross margin rose from 58.6% to 67.7%, operating margin from 49.6% to 60.3%, and net profit margin from 42.7% to 55.6%.

TSM Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts

TSMC is making more revenue and profit than ever, and that's likely to continue for the next couple of years as the AI infrastructure build-out continues. news.Title: Wall Street ends higher as investors buy AI stocks; Microsoft rallies
news.Content:
By Noel Randewich and Johann M Cherian

Sept 25 (Reuters) - Wall Street ended higher on Friday, lifted by Microsoft and other AI-related technology stocks, while high oil prices and a recent surge in US Treasury yields kept investors on edge.

Gains in ‌the S&P 500 and Nasdaq capped a volatile week driven by uncertainty about what industries will win and lose from artificial ‌intelligence, and by concerns about the US war with Iran and a surge in US Treasury yields.

Microsoft rallied 3.7%, lifting its 2026 gain to 7%, after the software giant ​unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent.

Chip maker Qualcomm gained 4% and Dell advanced 5%.

Akamai Technologies rallied 3.2% after an $11.6 billion cloud services deal with AI leader Anthropic. The deal includes a warrant that could give Anthropic up to 5% of Akamai.

"That's a positive from the standpoint that people are still investing, deals are still being done," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments ‌in Atlanta. "It's another circular deal, so OK ... but ⁠Akamai stock is up."

Meta Platforms dipped 3.3%. The social media company's stock soared about 13% this week amid a strong reception to its Muse AI agent, which analysts say could benefit tech infrastructure stocks, while challenging banks, online ⁠shopping platforms and other consumer businesses.

The S&P 500 climbed 0.51% to end the session at 7,743.41 points.

The Nasdaq gained 0.48% to 27,068.72 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.93% to 51,828.62 points.

Seven of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by information technology, up 0.91%, followed by a 0.6% ​gain ​in industrials.

The S&P 500 gained 1.2% for the week, while the Nasdaq rose 2% ​for the week after it notched a record-high close ‌on Tuesday.

The S&P 500 this week has traded just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights are responsible for much of the recent increase in earnings expectations.

A report that US and Iranian negotiators continued to explore a phased path out of the war, which would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade, helped market sentiment.

Data also showed strong AI-related capital expenditures boosted demand for key manufactured capital goods, outpacing expectations in August.

Brent crude eased but remained above $100 a barrel. The yield on ‌the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note hit a fresh 19-year high and was ​last up 3.4 basis points at 5.196%.

Story Continues

Traders see a 66% chance of the Federal ​Reserve increasing interest rates by at least 25 basis points in ​October, up from around 50% earlier this week, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.

US President Donald Trump said he ‌had a "very productive meeting" with President Xi Jinping, following ​a three-day summit that showcased personal diplomacy ​rather than big breakthroughs in economic relations.

Magazine publisher People Inc jumped 11% after a report said MGM Resorts International was discussing a bid for the company.

Volume on US exchanges was relatively light, with 14.9 billion shares traded, compared with an average of 16.8 ​billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

Advancing issues outnumbered ‌falling ones within the S&P 500 by a 1.9-to-one ratio.

The S&P 500 posted three new highs and 31 new lows; ​the Nasdaq recorded 54 new highs and 175 new lows.

(Reporting by Johann M Cherian and Avinash P in Bengaluru and ​Noel Randewich in San Francisco; Editing by Joyjeet Das and Matthew Lewis)

news.Title: HSBC Just Downgraded Twilio Stock. Here's Why.
news.Content:
Twilio (TWLO) stock tumbled on Friday after HSBC downgraded the cloud communications firm, warning that market excitement surrounding Meta Platforms' (META) new artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure might be misplaced. Analyst Sameer Lam lowered his rating on TWLO to "Reduce" and left his price target unchanged at $211, indicating potential downside of about 25% from current levels.

His bearish call arrives at a time when Twilio shares are in a relentless uptrend, currently trading at about 2x the price at which they started this year.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on Microsoft Stock

Mark Cuban Says He's 'All for Universal Care' But Warns It Won't 'Automagically Work,' and the 'Best First Step' Is This Warren-Hawley Bill

A $1.2 Billion Reason to Buy Lockheed Martin Stock

Get exclusive insights with the FREE Barchart Brief newsletter. Subscribe now for quick, incisive midday market analysis you won't find anywhere else.

Why Is HSBC Bearish on Twilio Stock

Investors have recently embraced Twilio as the backbone powering Meta Platforms' fast-growing AI voice and messaging ecosystem, Muse.

But Lam cautions that markets may be significantly overestimating how much bottom-line value actually flows back to the CPaaS pioneer.

While Muse will likely drive higher overall interaction volumes — from automated voice calls to security authentications — META retains tight ownership over its proprietary AI voice architecture.

By controlling the intelligent core of its AI assistant, the titan effectively limits TWLO's capacity to capture high-margin, value-added revenues.

Note that TWLO stock has a history of closing October in the red, a seasonal trend that further dulls its near-term appeal.

Twilio's Exposure to Meta's Ecosystem

Analyzing Twilio's technical exposure to Meta's ecosystem, HSBC points out that its primary role is relegated to basic public switched telephone network (PSTN) connectivity and transactional messaging.

These underlying infrastructure layers suffer from heavy commoditization, exposing the company to intense rivalry from providers like Bandwidth and Sinch that offer equivalent or more deeply integrated PSTN routing.

Plus, Meta retains the flexibility to bypass third-party aggregators altogether by establishing direct wholesale SIP trunking links with global telecommunications carriers.

In short, analyst Sameer Lam noted that rising artificial intelligence traffic across the sector "does not guarantee Twilio captures disproportionate economics."

Story Continues

Wall Street Remains Bullish on TWLO Shares

Other Wall Street analysts do not really agree with Lam's bearish view on TWLO shares, though.

The consensus rating on Twilio remains at "Strong Buy," with price targets as high as $330 indicating potential for another 20% rally from here.

news.Title: Meta Stock Surges 11% on AI Monetization Hopes
news.Content:
As tech giants have continued to pour billions of dollars into the current artificial intelligence (AI) landscape, skepticism has grown over when those massive investments will start paying dividends — or whether there will be any dividends at all. Today, however, the market narrative is shifting as companies start demonstrating viable revenue streams from AI. Meta Platforms (META) is one such company that has unveiled plans for AI-related revenue.

Meta Platforms is a global tech and social media powerhouse operating platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Threads, and more under its "Family of Apps." Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, Meta has also started to aggressively pivot toward the use of artificial intelligence, custom silicon, and consumer AI products like Muse and Meta AI. Let's take a closer look.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on Microsoft Stock

Mark Cuban Says He's 'All for Universal Care' But Warns It Won't 'Automagically Work,' and the 'Best First Step' Is This Warren-Hawley Bill

A $1.2 Billion Reason to Buy Lockheed Martin Stock

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Meta Stock Bounces Back

META stock has staged a dramatic comeback after experiencing some turbulence in the market in 2026. On Sept. 21, the stock shot higher by more than 11%, then set a new 52-week high of $779.82 on Sept. 24 after months of underperformance.

Shares of META were falling on a year-to-date (YTD) basis earlier this year, weighed down by soaring AI investments and disappointing second-quarter figures. However, the launch of Muse AI has helped ignite a powerful rally in the stock, with shares now up 14% YTD.

By comparison, the S&P 500 Communications Services Sector ($SRTS) — which includes major telecom and media names — has posted modest gains for much of the year. Meta's recent spike and AI-driven rally have helped the stock outperform even its own sector, underscoring investment sentiment.

Meta Reports Q2 Results

Meta Platforms reported its second-quarter 2026 results on July 29. The company showed revenue of $60.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year (YOY) and edging past the $60.2 billion analyst consensus estimate. However, diluted EPS came in at $6.18, missing the $7.22 estimate by more than 14% and snapping a streak of earnings beats as surging AI-related costs overwhelmed strong top-line growth.

Total costs and expenses surged 55% YOY to $42.03 billion, including $2.4 billion in legal charges and $1.18 billion in severance tied to an 8,000-employee headcount reduction, compressing Meta's GAAP operating margin to 31% from 43% a year earlier. Advertising revenue climbed 27% YOY to $59.36 billion, with ad impressions up 14% and average price per ad up 12%. Meanwhile, free cash flow plunged 91% YOY to just $784 million as capital expenditures hit $31.1 billion for the quarter.

Story Continues

Management guided Q3 revenue to $61 billion to $64 billion, while Wall Street estimates revenue of about $63 billion for the quarter. The company also narrowed its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $130 billion to $145 billion. CEO Mark Zuckerberg said that AI is "accelerating our core business today […] and opening the door to entirely new enterprise opportunities," while executives highlighted early traction from Meta's new enterprise AI cloud offering and the viral consumer adoption of Muse as key emerging monetization pathways.

Meta Gears up AI Monetization

Shares of Meta Platforms spiked more than 11% on Monday following investor enthusiasm surrounding the company's AI monetization strategy. The rally outpaced the broader tech space even as the S&P 500 Communications Services Sector popped nearly 4%, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained close to 3%, and rival firms like Alphabet (GOOGL), Reddit (RDDT), Netflix (NFLX), and Pinterest (PINS) made similar small gains.

Meta's recent spike continued its rally from early September, when it jumped following the initial Muse AI rollout and its acquisition of Swedish startup Stilla.ai.

Analysts have increasingly linked these catalysts to Meta's potential to unlock revenue streams beyond traditional digital advertising, including subscriptions, transactions, and business messaging monetization across WhatsApp, Messenger, and Instagram. That's reinforcing growing confidence that Meta's massive AI investments are beginning to translate into tangible, diversified growth.

Should You Buy META Stock?

Meta Platforms' explosive rally around Muse and broader AI monetization prospects has reignited investor confidence that the company's massive AI investments are finally translating into diversified revenue streams beyond advertising.

Wall Street remains overwhelmingly bullish. Overall, META stock holds a consensus "Strong Buy" rating from 54 analysts with coverage. Out of those analysts, 45 have a "Strong Buy" rating, two have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and seven have a "Hold" rating. The average price target of $786.74 implies modest potential upside of about 4% from current levels, suggesting the recent surge has largely caught up to analyst expectations even as long-term AI-monetization optimism remains strong.

news.Title: Microsoft Just Raised Its Dividend by 8%: Is It the Best Magnificent Seven Dividend to Own?
news.Content:
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) has lagged the broader market over the past 12 months, as some investors fear that the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution will eventually decrease demand for the company's services. However, there are still many things to like about the tech leader, including its dividend program. In fact, Microsoft recently announced it was raising its dividend by 8%. How does the company's income program compare to those of its similarly-sized peers that are members of the Magnificent Seven? Let's find out.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Microsoft's attractive dividend program

On Sept. 15, Microsoft announced that it was increasing its quarterly dividend per share to $0.98. It's worth noting that even before this increase, the company's dividend was much higher than the average for the Magnificent Seven members with dividend programs, including Meta Platforms , Apple , Alphabet , and Nvidia .

In fact, the next highest quarterly dividend per share is Meta's $0.525, a little over half of Microsoft's new $0.98. Of course, this is a per-share metric and therefore doesn't tell us much. Since share prices differ, a lower dividend per share could still equate to a higher yield. But Microsoft has averaged a higher yield than its peers in this group over the past decade, and it still beats them in this category.

We can also look beyond this metric. And once we do, we see a similar picture. For instance, Meta and Alphabet have only been paying dividends for a few years. Apple and Nvidia are longtime dividend payers, but neither has a track record of dividend growth as impressive as Microsoft's. Although Nvidia recently increased its dividend significantly, it went many years without a single annual hike.

That's not the case with Microsoft, which has grown its dividend regularly for over a decade. Apple also has, but Microsoft's dividend growth has been more impressive over the past 10 years. Further, Microsoft has a cash payout ratio (the percentage of cash flow paid as dividends) of 39.5%, compared to Apple's 15.6%. Generally, the lower a cash payout ratio, the better. But when it is too low, it can indicate that the company has other priorities, including some that may also benefit investors, such as share buybacks.

Story Continues

That might be the case with Apple. Microsoft's cash payout ratio, on the other hand, is well within a healthy range. The bottom line: Microsoft appears to have a much stronger dividend program than its peers in the Magnificent Seven.

Can the business support more dividend growth?

If the bears are right and Microsoft's services eventually experience significantly lower demand due to AI disruption, the company's dividend program may suffer as well. But how likely is that? In my view, not very. Consider Microsoft's latest financial results for the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 2026, which ended June 30. Microsoft's revenue increased by 18% year over year to $90 billion. The company's non-GAAP earnings per share (which excludes the impact of investments in OpenAI ) were $4.74, up 23% compared to the year-ago period.

Of course, we can't make too much out of a single quarter. But Microsoft's update showed plenty of signs of strong, sustained demand for its services, particularly in its cloud business. Microsoft Cloud revenue came in at $59.3 billion, up 27% year over year, and the company ended the period with $678 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations, 84% higher than the prior-year quarter. As management pointed out, AI is playing a key role in boosting cloud revenue, and there is more where that came from, judging by Microsoft's significant backlog.

The company is also showing that it can coexist with AI. Microsoft has launched various AI agents that cater to its clients' needs. Improving its services through AI can enable the company to continue capitalizing on the AI revolution over the medium term, potentially leading to consistent revenue and earnings growth. Microsoft could also see improved margins as it increasingly relies on custom AI chips, which can lower its AI computing costs. Microsoft has survived several technological revolutions over its long and storied history.

AI is unlikely to be its undoing. Lastly, we could point to Microsoft's rock-solid balance sheet. The company boasts an AAA credit rating -- the highest possible rating -- from S&P Global, strong evidence that it is more than capable of meeting its financial obligations. All of these factors and more highlight the strength of Microsoft's underlying operations and its excellent prospects in cloud computing and AI. And with a business that healthy, we can expect consistent dividend growth for a long time.

news.Title: Sundar Pichai Reported Alphabet's Cloud Backlog Hit $514 Billion After 82% Revenue Growth Last Quarter, With Nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 Using Gemini Enterprise. Is Google Cloud Becoming a Bigger Growth Driver Than Search?
news.Content:
Tech sector investors already knew Google Cloud was growing rapidly, but even most bulls were not prepared for the magnitude of growth that showed up in Alphabet 's (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) second-quarter results. Cloud revenue surged by 82% year over year, and on the earnings call, CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the unit's $514 billion backlog.

AI has been a major component of Alphabet's recent success, with nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies using Gemini Enterprise. Alphabet has long been known for its ubiquitous search engine, but cloud computing may be more important than search in future earnings reports.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Google Cloud's slice of the pie has gotten much bigger

It wasn't that long ago that Google Cloud accounted for only a small slice of Alphabet's total revenue. Investors waited for the unit's losses to minimize and yearned for the day when Google Cloud would become profitable. Its first profitable quarter arrived in 2023, and now, it's a major part of the business.

Google Cloud made up 14% of total revenue in Q2 2025, but its ongoing AI-fueled growth spurt has boosted its share to a little more than 20% of total revenue. Its 82% growth rate and $514 billion backlog are far more exciting figures for investors to consider than Alphabet's 14% year-over-year growth in advertising revenue.

The magnitude of the backlog reflects that demand for cloud capacity is still heating up. Alphabet is sitting on a lot of promised revenue that it still has to realize. It's feasible that Google Cloud could make up more than one-quarter of the company's total revenue next year.

Google Cloud's growing influence also comes at a time when its net operating income more than tripled year over year. The Google services segment, which mostly consists of online ads, only posted a 20% improvement.

It's gaining ground on Amazon and Microsoft

Alphabet is one of the big three cloud infrastructure providers. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) has the largest market share -- 28% at last report -- and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) is in second place with 21%.

However, Google Cloud is growing faster than the other tech giants' offerings. Alphabet currently has a 14% market share, up from 12% as of Q4 2025. If current growth rates hold, it's feasible that Alphabet could claim the silver medal within a few years.

Story Continues

Dethroning Amazon Web Services -- if that's possible -- would take quite a bit longer, since there's such a wide gap between the leader and its peers. While Amazon Web Services' growth has reaccelerated, it's still much slower than Google Cloud's growth rates.

Alphabet's ability to grow faster than the other two cloud providers shows it is more often the preferred choice for existing and new customers that are seeking more AI infrastructure.

Amazon and Microsoft are sitting on market share leads they established long before the AI boom. More recent results point to Google Cloud gaining more market share, and its growth being more impactful than Google Search's on Alphabet's overall financial picture.

news.Title: Why Intel Stock Jumped This Week
news.Content:
Shares of Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) were rising this week, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence . The semiconductor maker is seeing rising enthusiasm due to the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence ( AI ) agents that could require massive amounts of compute to run.

Intel stock climbed 14.3% this week and is now up over 250% in the past year. Here's why, and whether the stock might be a buy from here.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Agentic usage and partnerships

The talk of the town over the last week has been the release of Meta Platforms' AI agent, Muse. Muse can perform legitimate tasks for users, such as booking flights, saving money by canceling subscriptions, or making restaurant reservations. It has shot up the mobile app stores, garnering millions of downloads in just a few weeks since launch.

For Intel, rising usage of AI agents could mean more usage from its computer chips in data centers, which is why the stock was rising this week. Intel has been struggling for years to compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, and the AI boom may just give it a bounce-back in demand, helping it regain a solid footing.

Is Intel stock a buy?

Intel's revenue grew 25% year-over-year last quarter, and it now has partnerships with many players across the semiconductor supply chain, as well as backing from the U.S. government. The stock is not cheap today, but if you believe in the long-term growth of the AI infrastructure build-out, Intel stock will probably do fine over the next decade.

news.Title: Microsoft Revamps Copilot as AI Spending Scrutiny Grows
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Microsoft ( MSFT ) is overhauling Copilot with a stronger focus on enterprise customers , rolling out a unified assistant that combines consumer and workplace capabilities while giving companies more control over how employees use and pay for artificial intelligence.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with MSFT.

Is MSFT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The redesign has been in development for roughly six months and begins rolling out through Microsoft's Frontier program.

The new Copilot app is organized around several major features.

Home brings together Chat and Cowork, while Code lets users build and run software using GitHub Copilot technology. Autopilot, previously called Scout, functions as a persistent agent designed to act proactively for users.

But the most important addition for large companies may be FinOps for AI.

Microsoft says the tool is designed to help organizations track AI usage, control spending and connect that spending to business value.

FinOps for AI is a shared discipline for managing AI spend and optimizing it for business value, said Jared Spataro, chief marketing officer for Microsoft AI at Work.

Administrators will be able to manage spending policies at scale, route requests for additional AI credits through existing approval systems, and decide which model families different employee groups can access.

That matters as enterprise AI adoption becomes more expensive and complex.

Microsoft is effectively trying to make Copilot not just the interface employees use for AI, but also the management layer companies use to govern it.

The timing is notable. Meta is gaining attention with its Muse personal AI agent, while Qualcomm has introduced platforms designed to support personal agents across devices.

Investor takeaway

For Microsoft investors, the Copilot overhaul shifts the monetization discussion toward enterprise control and recurring usage.

The key question is whether companies see enough productivity gains to increase AI spending rather than limit it.

Investors should watch Copilot adoption, paid seat growth, agent usage, Azure consumption and whether FinOps tools reduce enterprise resistance to rising AI costs.

The biggest opportunity is that Microsoft already owns much of the software stack enterprises use every day.

If Copilot becomes the layer companies use to deploy, monitor and budget AI agents, Microsoft could capture more value from AI spending without relying solely on model access itself.

Microsoft plans to unveil additional Copilot features at Ignite from November 17 through November 20.

news.Title: The Dow Leads Market Indexes Higher as Microsoft Adds 120 Points
news.Content:
Stocks rose Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES: ^DJI) leading. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) decided it doesn't want to build your personal AI assistant after all, and investors loved it. Meta (NASDAQ: META) absolutely wants to build your personal AI assistant, and the Muse maker had a worse morning.

The Dow rose 0.8% as of 12:49 p.m. ET. The Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) gained 0.5%, and the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) added 0.4%. Nineteen of the Dow's 30 components traded higher.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

^DJI data by YCharts

Microsoft gave up on consumer AI to investor applause

Microsoft was the leading driver of the major indexes' bullish moves this morning. The software giant jumped 4.1% and added 120 Dow points after merging its consumer and workplace Copilot apps into one enterprise product. Translation: Microsoft is ceding the personal chatbot market to OpenAI, Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), and Meta so it can focus on a more lucrative customer class.

Meta took the other side of that bet and dropped 3.6%, losing most of Thursday's 4.3% gain. The Facebook and Instagram parent laid out plans to put its Muse agent into AI glasses, previewed a pocket-sized gadget called Charm, and promised more than 100 styles of Muse-driven glasses by year-end. Investors were unimpressed.

In the hardware sector, memory-chip giant SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY) rose 3% after the Taiwanese media outlet DigiTimes reported that the company is in the running for significant memory orders as Sony (NYSE: SONY) assembles the next PlayStation console. Sector rival Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) held steady with a 0.2% price drop as investors brace for next week's earnings report.

And this mid-day market review can never ignore the oil trade. The United States Oil Fund (NYSEMKT: USO) dropped 3.2% after Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within seven days and that nuclear talks could restart, provided Washington meets his conditions. Brent crude prices slipped 1% lower to $105 per barrel.

Don't celebrate at the pump just yet

Here's the catch in Araghchi's offer. His conditions are the same as those in the June 17 memorandum of understanding, and the Trump administration has already said it won't return to those terms. That deal also fell apart within weeks of being signed. Araghchi said Iran isn't in a hurry, while acknowledging that a deal before the midterms would probably be better for everyone involved.

Story Continues

Don't expect the pump to catch up quickly either. Regular gas averages $4.49 per gallon today, up roughly 10% in a month and 42% in a year, and diesel is $6.50 per gallon after hitting a record $6.53 on Tuesday. Fuel prices follow crude with a lag, so one day of falling oil doesn't necessarily fix anything at your local gas station right away.

Two Dow gainers had no explanation to speak of. Caterpillar (NYSE: CAT) added 73 points on a 1.5% rise and Sherwin-Williams (NYSE: SHW) contributed 49 more on a 2.6% gain, neither with company news attached. Both are cyclical names that tend to move with the economy rather than their own announcements. And their beefy share prices result in heavy Dow weightings, currently totaling about 13% of the total index score.

Seven days is a short deadline for a war in its seventh month. The market seems to be in an optimistic mode about these discussions, though. Next week brings Micron's earnings, followed by the discussion deadline.

news.Title: Quantum Selloff: Should Investors Consider These 3 Hyperscalers?
news.Content:
The quantum-computing trade is facing a valuation reset as investors demand clearer evidence of commercialization. Over the past few months, pure-play quantum computing stocks have come under pressure despite technological milestones, partnerships and government backing. The market is essentially skeptical about one key issue: quantum progress is accelerating, but the revenue and earnings needed to justify lofty valuations remain further out.

Yet the broader quantum space has been performing much better than the pure plays. The Defiance Quantum ETF QTUM, which holds a diversified basket spanning quantum, AI, semiconductors and technology infrastructure, delivered more than 40% growth over the past six months.

This gives investors a reason to reassess how they want to participate in the quantum opportunity. Pure plays offer more direct exposure, but their investment cases remain closely tied to future quantum adoption. By contrast, hyperscalers are already generating substantial revenue from cloud and AI while investing in quantum research and infrastructure.

Here, we have selected three hyperscaler stocks, Alphabet GOOGL, Amazon AMZN and Microsoft MSFT, that combine established revenue streams with expanding quantum-computing initiatives.

Quantum Opportunity Still There

Rather than relying solely on companies whose valuations depend heavily on future quantum commercialization, investors can examine hyperscalers that are already monetizing cloud and AI infrastructure while building quantum capabilities. That combination provides a different way to participate in quantum's longer-term development without making quantum revenue the immediate earnings driver.

Why Hyperscalers Remain in Focus

The 2026 selloff in pure-play quantum stocks reflects a growing focus on when companies can generate meaningful cash flows, not whether quantum technology is advancing. IonQ, Rigetti and D-Wave continue to report technology and commercial milestones, but their investment cases remain tied closely to future quantum adoption. Higher federal reserve rates add to the pressure.

Meanwhile, the solid ETF performance shows that investors are not necessarily abandoning quantum exposure but are becoming more selective about companies that can benefit from the theme while generating revenue from established businesses.

That backdrop puts hyperscalers in focus. Their AI and cloud operations provide current revenue streams that can support longer-duration quantum investments, reducing reliance on near-term quantum monetization. Meanwhile, government funding continues to target the industry's technical bottlenecks. The Commerce Department finalized up to $100 million each for Rigetti and D-Wave on Sept. 8, while a separate award of up to $1 billion to IBM's newly formed Anderon subsidiary is aimed at establishing a quantum semiconductor foundry.

Story Continues

3 Hyperscalers to Consider

Alphabet: The company combines strong cloud growth with an expanding quantum program. Alphabet's second-quarter 2026 revenue increased 24% year over year, while Google Cloud revenue surged 82%. Google Quantum AI is pursuing both superconducting and neutral-atom approaches and said in March that it expects commercially relevant superconducting quantum computers by the end of the decade. In July, Google researchers also reported progress in using reinforcement learning to improve quantum error correction.

GOOGL carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The stock is expected to report earnings growth of 89.7% in 2026 over revenue growth of 26.4%.

Amazon: Amazon offers quantum exposure through AWS alongside strong AI infrastructure growth. AWS sales jumped 37% year over year in the second quarter, its fastest growth in 18 quarters, while AWS operating income rose to $16.6 billion. AWS also reached a $169 billion annualized revenue run rate, while its AI business and Amazon's chips business each surpassed $25 billion in annualized revenues. Separately, AWS and QuEra plan to bring the Libra fault-tolerant quantum system to Amazon Braket in 2028.

AMZN carries a Zacks Rank #3. The stock is expected to report 2026 earnings growth of 81.5% on revenue growth of 15.7%.

Microsoft: The company combines strong Azure growth with a differentiated topological-qubit approach. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 39% in fiscal second-quarter 2026. More recently, on Sept. 22, Microsoft opened a 15,000-square-foot quantum research center in Maryland, giving DARPA direct on-site access to its Majorana 2 quantum system for independent testing and evaluation.

MSFT carries a Zacks Rank #3. The stock is expected to report fiscal 2027 earnings growth of 9.3% on revenue growth of 17.4%. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Why It’s Time to Buy Alphabet Stock
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) stock has underperformed the broader equity market so far in 2026. Shares of the Google parent have gained about 10% year-to-date (YTD), compared with a 13% increase in the S&P 500 ($SPX).

While Alphabet stock has underperformed the broader market, the tech giant's growth outlook remains solid. The tech giant is well positioned for strong growth, supported by diversified revenue streams and expanding exposure to several high-growth markets.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on Microsoft Stock

SpaceX's Weight in the Nasdaq-100 Is Set to Double, But There Are More Important Catalysts to Watch for SPCX Stock

Mark Cuban Says He's 'All for Universal Care' But Warns It Won't 'Automagically Work,' and the 'Best First Step' Is This Warren-Hawley Bill

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

Alphabet's strong cloud backlog points to sustained demand for Google Cloud Platform (GCP), while expanding adoption of its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) creates a substantial opportunity as demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure accelerates.

Alphabet will also benefit from its growing subscription ecosystem, which provides recurring revenue. Meanwhile, the continued resilience of its core Search business and higher engagement on YouTube will support its advertising revenue, providing significant cash and strengthening its ability to fund investments in AI and other growth initiatives.

Alphabet's Diversified Growth Engines Strengthen Investment Case

Alphabet's growth outlook remains solid, driven by its diversified revenue base, including cloud, AI, advertising, and subscription businesses. While advertising continues to provide a substantial earnings base, the rapid expansion of Google Cloud and growing monetization of AI-related products are creating additional sources of revenue and profit growth.

While Alphabet is investing significantly in AI capabilities, the move is accelerating its growth. The most significant evidence that Alphabet's infrastructure investments are beginning to pay off is the acceleration in Google Cloud. Cloud revenue climbed 82% year over year to $24.8 billion in the second quarter, compared with 63% growth in the first quarter. The acceleration reflects stronger demand for GCP, AI infrastructure, and enterprise AI solutions.

The improvement in profitability is particularly notable. Google Cloud generated $8.8 billion in operating income, more than three times the prior-year level. Its operating margin expanded from 20.7% to 35.6%.

Story Continues

Looking ahead, Alphabet's expanding Cloud backlog supports the growth outlook. Its backlog increased by more than $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion. The company also began recognizing revenue from TPU systems deployed in customers' data centers during the second quarter. TPUs represent another solid avenue for Alphabet to monetize its AI infrastructure capabilities.

Management expects only a relatively small portion of revenue from existing TPU system agreements to be recognized in the current year, with recognition expected to accelerate as the company exits 2026. Management expects to realize the substantial majority of revenue associated with these agreements in 2027. Consequently, TPU-related revenue could become a more meaningful contributor to Alphabet's financial performance over the next several years.

At the same time, Alphabet's core advertising business continues to demonstrate resilience. Google Search and other advertising revenue increased 17% year over year to $63.3 billion in the second quarter, while YouTube advertising revenue grew 13% to $11.1 billion.

The growing integration of AI into Search is driving user engagement and supporting advertising monetization.

In addition, Alphabet's revenue diversification extends beyond advertising and Cloud. Subscription, platforms, and devices revenue increased 15% in the second quarter, supported by growth in YouTube subscriptions and Google One.

YouTube Music and YouTube Premium continued to drive subscription expansion, while Google One benefited from rising demand for AI-focused plans. This creates an additional monetization channel for Alphabet's AI investments.

Overall, Alphabet is well-positioned to deliver strong growth ahead, led by its diversified revenue base and acceleration in its cloud business.

Valuation Indicates Room for Upside

Alphabet's valuation appears relatively undemanding given its growth prospects. GOOGL stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 17.1x, notably lower than several large technology peers. By comparison, Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN) trade at forward P/E multiples of 25.4 and 31.8, respectively.

Although elevated capital expenditure could weigh on margins and free cash flow in the near term, these investments are strengthening Alphabet's competitive position and accelerating its growth.

Its solid growth trajectory and relatively low valuation suggest further upside in GOOGL stock.

Alphabet Stock Is a Buy Now

Alphabet's accelerating Cloud business, expanding AI monetization, resilient advertising, and growing subscription revenue provide a diversified base for solid growth ahead. While elevated AI-related capital spending may pressure near-term margins and free cash flow, the resulting infrastructure investments are strengthening Alphabet's position in high-growth markets.

With shares trading at about 17.1 times forward earnings, Alphabet appears reasonably priced against its expected growth and valuations across other large-cap technology companies, adding to its investment appeal.

Analysts remain positive on the company, with Alphabet's stock currently sporting a "Strong Buy" consensus rating.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Meta's popular AI agent

On Sept. 8, Meta Platforms released Muse, an AI agent designed to help people accomplish various tasks by constantly working in the background. Muse goes beyond the question-and-answer format of AI chatbots and can proactively work toward goals and take things off its users' to-do lists. The release of Muse was hardly a surprise. Meta's CEO, Mark Zuckerberg , had explicitly said that his vision of AI included personalized agents. But would people embrace this vision? We now have a tentative answer to that question, and it is in the affirmative.

Five days after Muse's release, it topped the U.S. App Store's list of the most popular free apps. It had already recorded about 730,000 downloads. This provides some evidence that AI agents could become highly popular. Meta's spending on AI infrastructure enabled the company to build increasingly capable AI models, which now power products such as Muse, a sophisticated AI agent. But this could only be the beginning for Meta Platforms. We can likely expect Muse to become increasingly capable, and perhaps Meta will launch other AI agents in the future.

How could this affect the company's financial results? Muse is free to download and use within certain limits; beyond that, there are paid subscription tiers. Provided Meta can get enough paid subscribers, it could become a meaningful source of revenue for the company. We are not there yet, of course, but these recent developments paint a much brighter future for Meta than its stock performance over the past 12 months suggests. It's not surprising that the stock has soared by more than 20% since it released Muse.

Story Continues

Is Meta stock a buy?

Meta's AI spending has been intentional, and although it has weighed on short-term profits and free cash flow (with other factors also affecting its recent profitability), the company is now showing the potential of its strategy. There could be more in the near future. Meta has reportedly been looking to sell excess AI computing capacity. Management pointed out that, given the current demand for these services, the company could sell compute at a significant premium over what it paid for it.

Meanwhile, the core advertising business remains healthy, and Meta continues to grow its ecosystem. Second-quarter revenue increased by 28% year over year to $60.8 billion, while daily active people came in at 3.60 billion, 3% higher than the year-ago period. Meta's deep ecosystem is a strong competitive advantage, offering it numerous monetization opportunities. Lastly, the company has moved closer to addressing another issue.

Meta has faced lawsuits over alleged social media harm, but it recently reached a settlement with many of the plaintiffs. Meta agreed to pay about $18 billion over a 10-year period -- a fairly small amount for a company that generates more than $60 billion in annual profits -- and put more guardrails on its websites and apps to protect young users. For all those reasons, Meta's stock looks attractive for investors willing to hold onto it for the long term.

The best Magnificent Seven stock?

Meta might be an attractive stock to buy, but whether it's the best Magnificent Seven stock right now is another question. The Magnificent Seven group includes Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA). Some of them are performing particularly well, even as they have also declined meaningfully over the past 12 months. That's the case with Microsoft, for instance. Meanwhile, the likes of Alphabet and Nvidia are seeing accelerating sales growth and boast outstanding medium-term prospects, given the AI industry's rapid expansion.

We could also point out Apple's recent launch of the iPhone 18 and the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, which may prove extremely popular. Is Meta really a better stock to buy than all of them? I don't think so. Nvidia in particular looks highly attractive. It has a near-impregnable moat in its core GPU (graphics processing unit) market, continues to post outstanding results, and has expanded its product portfolio to capitalize on the agentic AI boom. Yet, the market still underestimates the semiconductor specialist.

Meta and Nvidia are both in my portfolio, but if I had to pick just one to double down on right now, it would be the latter.

news.Title: Generac Is Becoming an AI Power Play. Amazon Just Made That Case Bigger.
news.Content:
Generac (GNRC), best-known for supplying backup generators for homes, has been building a bigger presence in the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market for years — and Amazon (AMZN) just gave the company a major opportunity. Under the deal, Generac is set to provide roughly $2.4 billion in generators to Amazon over 2027 and 2028, while the partnership has room to expand to as much as $8 billion. Amazon also received a warrant to acquire up to 1.69 million Generac shares with a potential exercise value of about $340 million.

GNRC stock has climbed 50% so far this year, while Amazon stock is up 8% year-to-date (YTD). The deal sounds like a win-win for both companies. But does that make Generac stock a buy now?

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on Microsoft Stock

Why SoFi Stock Is a Good Buy Now

Anthropic's CEO Warned of AI Risks and Accenture Found a Business Opportunity There. How to Play ACN Stock Now.

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

Amazon Is Turning Generac Into an AI Infrastructure Story

Generac was already moving toward data centers before Amazon entered the picture. In the second quarter, sales for its Commercial & Industrial business rose 29% to $556 million. This growth was driven by increasing shipments of "products sold to the data center market." AI data centers need enormous amounts of electricity, backup generators, and other power infrastructure to keep critical computing equipment operating when grid power is interrupted or unavailable. Generac's large megawatt generators are specifically designed to meet that need.

Furthermore, on the Q2 earnings call, management also stated that the company has a path to triple large MW production capacity over the following 12 months. The company is also accelerating work at its Sussex, Wisconsin, facility and expanding packaging capacity, including through its facility in Belvidere, Illinois.

Generac already had $1.6 billion of data-center orders waiting to be delivered at the end of Q2. Amazon's deal adds another major customer to that growing business, giving Generac another potential source of future growth as Amazon expands its AI data centers.

The $340 Million Warrant Explains How

Amazon also got a piece of the upside with the Generac deal.

The upside comes from the $340 million warrant that gives Amazon the right to potentially acquire up to 1.69 million shares of Generac common stock at an exercise price of $200.93 per share. If Amazon ultimately exercises the entire warrant for cash, Generac could receive roughly $340 million in proceeds, with Amazon receiving an equity stake in a rising AI infrastructure company. However, while Generac will receive additional cash when the warrants are exercised, it will also dilute existing shareholders.

Story Continues

Amazon's benefit goes beyond the potential equity upside. From this deal, Amazon gains a long-term relationship with Generac for backup power rather than relying solely on spot orders or sourcing generators project by project. This is particularly important for Amazon, whose data-center footprint is rapidly expanding to support AI and cloud workloads.

Is Generac Stock a Buy Now?

Generac's earnings growth estimates over the next two years make its valuation look reasonable. Analysts estimate that EPS will rise to $9.74 in fiscal 2026, a 54% increase, while revenue is expected to climb 17% to $4.9 billion. Furthermore, revenue is expected to increase 27% to about $6.2 billion in fiscal 2027, while EPS is expected to rise 22% to $11.92. Trading at 17.4 times forward 2027 earnings, investors are paying a relatively moderate price for the projected growth.

Furthermore, the Amazon agreement adds another potential growth catalyst, with $2.4 billion of initial generator deliveries expected in 2027 and 2028. Amazon's new equity link with Generac could further strengthen the company's emerging AI infrastructure story.

On Wall Street, GNRC stock holds a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating. Of the 20 analysts that cover the stock, 13 have a "Strong Buy," one analyst has a "Moderate Buy," and six have a "Hold" rating. The average target price of $295.69 implies that GNRC stock could climb 42% from current levels. Meanwhile, the high price estimate of $375 suggests potential upside of around 80% over the next 12 months.

news.Title: Microsoft CEO: We 'have to earn that permission' to build data centers from communities
news.Content:
The AI data center build-out has turned Nvidia ( NVDA ) into a $5 trillion company, is helping to power Intel's ( INTC ) turnaround effort s , and made memory chip makers some of the hottest companies on Earth.

But a growing number of Americans see the boom as a burden being forced upon them that is gobbling up land, power, and water. Coupled with non-disclosure agreements that some companies require towns to sign, the situation has become volatile.

An increasing number of states have introduced legislation halting or banning the construction of data centers, with New York issuing a state-wide, one-year moratorium. Texas has similarly blocked new data center projects until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) completes an audit to assess the facilities' impact on Texas's power grid and water resources.to halt or ban the construction of data centers, with New York issuing a statewide

To address the matter, Microsoft ( MSFT ) is taking a more open approach to its data center plans. In March, the company announced it was ending the use of non-disclosure agreements and terminating existing ones .

"At the end of the day, I think we have to get permission from the communities," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told Deirdre Bosa. "If you are going to be building a data center, consuming power, using water, at the end of the day, we have to earn that permission."

The move is part of what Microsoft calls its Community-First AI Infrastructure Plan . Unveiled in January, the effort includes the software giant paying to ensure electricity rates in data-center areas don't rise, minimizing and replenishing more water than the company uses, hiring local workers, not asking communities to reduce taxes on data centers, and investing in AI training.

"We have a set of commitments, right? I don't think of anything that we do as building a data center and getting out. No. It's about being able to be welcomed in the community on an ongoing basis," Nadella explained.

The CEO pointed to Microsoft's efforts in Quincy, Wash., as an example of how the company says it can move forward. Since Microsoft began constructing its first company-owned data center in 2006, Quincy's poverty rate has declined from 29.4% to 13.1% between 2012 and 2023.

Tax rates for residents have also declined, while the improved tax base has helped pay for a new hospital and other municipal facilities, according to Microsoft.

"They have a new hospital, they have a new school. They have a new city center. And over the years, we've also created a lot of employment opportunities. We have close to a thousand people there," Nadella said.

Story Continues

"And by the way, most people think of data centers as just something that's a construct, and then it's all autonomous. It's not the case because you're constantly refurbishing and building. And so ultimately, if you are contributing to the local economy and doing it in a way that benefits the people there, I think we'll have the permission."
